inspiration.observed_pattern: A MySQL date-function example subtracts a fixed interval from a date with SUBDATE alongside related temporal arithmetic functions.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Rewritten as an independently authored billing-cutoff audit. Fixed DATETIME anchors exercise day, month, quarter, year, and hour SUBDATE intervals, including leap-day month-end clamping and SQL NULL propagation; the source tables, values, dynamic clock, labels, and application purpose are new.

fixture_notes: Invoice 401 starts on 2024-03-31 so subtracting one month reaches leap-day February; invoice 402 crosses a year boundary; invoice 403 preserves SQL NULL through every SUBDATE projection.
determinism_notes: Invoice IDs, DATETIME anchors, and interval literals are fixed, and output is ordered by the primary key with no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections.
setup: CREATE TABLE billing_cutoffs (invoice_id INT PRIMARY KEY, invoice_label VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, issued_at DATETIME NULL)

steps.sql: SELECT invoice_id, invoice_label, issued_at, SUBDATE(issued_at, INTERVAL 10 DAY) AS day_cutoff, SUBDATE(issued_at, INTERVAL 1 MONTH) AS month_cutoff, SUBDATE(issued_at, INTERVAL 1 QUARTER) AS quarter_cutoff, SUBDATE(issued_at, INTERVAL 1 YEAR) AS year_cutoff, SUBDATE(issued_at, INTERVAL 2 HOUR) AS hour_cutoff FROM billing_cutoffs ORDER BY invoice_id
